_meta.purpose: Definitions for table column headers that carry no title of their own. js/components/table-header-tips.js looks a header up here by its normalized text (lowercase, whitespace collapsed) when the <th> has neither a title nor a data-tip. Headers that renderers annotate directly (ranking index, county comparison, projections, opportunity finder) do not need entries; entries here are fallbacks for static markup and shared headers.
_meta.normalization: trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase, strip trailing sort glyphs

tips.#: Row number in the current sort order.
tips.rank: Position in the current ranking, 1 = highest overall housing-need score among the jurisdictions shown.
tips.scenario rank: Position under the scenario weights you have set, compared with the official ranking.
tips.official rank: Position under the site's default, published weights.
tips.move: How many places this jurisdiction moved between the official ranking and your scenario ranking.
tips.score δ: Change in the overall need score between the official weights and your scenario weights.
tips.score change: Change in the overall need score between the official weights and your scenario weights.
tips.geography: The county, incorporated place, or census-designated place. Click the name to open its full assessment.
tips.type: County, incorporated place (city or town), or CDP (census-designated place — an unincorporated community the Census draws a boundary around).
tips.region: Colorado planning region the jurisdiction belongs to.
tips.full hna: Opens the complete Housing Needs Assessment for this jurisdiction.
tips.housing authority: Whether a public housing authority serves this jurisdiction.
tips.housing nonprofits: Whether housing-focused nonprofit organizations are active in this jurisdiction.
tips.housing needs assessment: Whether the jurisdiction has an adopted housing needs assessment on file.
tips.measure: The housing measure being compared. Each row is a rate — a share of households or units — never a count.
tips.difference: Jurisdiction minus county, in percentage points.
tips.dimension: The scoring dimension being compared across the selected jurisdictions.
tips.source: The public dataset or publisher the figure comes from.
tips.vintage: The data year or release the figure reflects. Older vintages are labeled so a reader can judge staleness.
tips.what it provides: The specific fields or signals this source contributes.
tips.scenario: Growth scenario: low, baseline, or high household projection. Read the three as a range.
tips.5-year need: Homes needed by year 5 to house projected new households at a healthy vacancy rate, cumulative from the base year. All incomes and tenures — not affordable-only, and not net of existing stock.
tips.10-year need: Same measure at year 10, cumulative from the base year.
tips.20-year need: Same measure at year 20, cumulative from the base year.
tips.annual gap: Average homes needed per year over the 20-year window. Compare against recent permitting pace.
tips.county (4-person household): Income limits are set per county and household size; four persons is HUD's reference household.
tips.30% ami: 30% of Area Median Income for a four-person household — the extremely-low-income limit.
tips.50% ami: 50% of Area Median Income — the very-low-income limit.
tips.60% ami: 60% of Area Median Income — the ceiling most tax-credit rental homes are priced to.
tips.80% ami: 80% of Area Median Income — the low-income limit used by most workforce and ownership programs.
tips.100% ami: The Area Median Income itself for a four-person household.
tips.states: Number of states in the region.
tips.state: The U.S. state this row describes.
tips.allocation: Annual Low-Income Housing Tax Credit authority allocated to the state, in dollars.
tips.total allocation: Combined annual tax-credit authority for all states in the region, in dollars.
tips.% of national: This row's share of the national tax-credit allocation.
tips.per-capita: Tax-credit allocation per resident. Each state receives a per-capita amount, with a small-state minimum.
tips.per capita: Tax-credit allocation per resident. Each state receives a per-capita amount, with a small-state minimum.
tips.population: Resident population used for the per-capita calculation.
tips.total: Sum of the column for all rows shown.
tips.target deal type: The financing structure the scoring weights are tuned for — 9% competitive, 4% bond, preservation, workforce/resort, or Prop 123 local.
tips.universe filter: Which jurisdictions are included before scoring — for example, only those with a QCT or DDA designation.
tips.co count: Number of Colorado jurisdictions that pass the universe filter.
tips.score: Composite score, 0–100, under the active target deal type's weights.
tips.band: Score range this letter grade covers.
tips.letter: Letter grade assigned to the score band — a reading aid, not a recommendation.
tips.interpretation: What a score in this band tends to mean, in plain language.
tips.out of scope: A situation the tool deliberately does not score.
tips.why: The reason it is out of scope.
tips.where to go instead: The page or source that does cover it.
tips.metric: The measure shown in this row.
tips.value: The measured value for this jurisdiction.
tips.notes: Caveats, method notes, or source detail for the row.
tips.jurisdiction: The county, city, town, or census-designated place.
tips.county: The Colorado county, or the county containing the selected place.
tips.median rent: Median gross rent — rent plus tenant-paid utilities — from the American Community Survey.
tips.median hh income: Median household income from the American Community Survey.
tips.acs vintage: The five-year American Community Survey release the row is drawn from, named by its final year.
tips.rent ÷ income: Share of pretax median household income spent on the median rent. Above 30% means the median renter is cost-burdened on the median home.
tips.renters burdened (30%+): Share of renter households paying 30% or more of income on rent and utilities.
tips.overall need score: Composite housing-need index, 0–100: cost burden, affordable-unit gap, affordability vs. local income, projected pressure and overcrowding, blended with an opportunity axis. Higher = more need.
tips.units needed (30% ami): Estimated shortfall of rental homes affordable to households earning up to 30% of area median income.
tips.% rent burdened: Share of renter households paying 30% or more of income on rent and utilities.
tips.in-commuters: Workers employed in the jurisdiction who live somewhere else (LEHD LODES) — a signal of workforce housing that isn't there.
tips.% renters: Share of occupied homes that are rented rather than owned.
tips.households: Number of households — occupied homes — from the American Community Survey.
tips.units needed (low): Homes needed under the low-growth projection scenario, cumulative from the base year.
tips.units needed (baseline): Homes needed under the baseline projection scenario, cumulative from the base year.
tips.units needed (high): Homes needed under the high-growth projection scenario, cumulative from the base year.
tips.units needed (custom): Homes needed under the growth assumptions you set in the scenario builder.
tips.project: Name of the development as recorded by CHFA.
tips.city: City or town where the development is located.
tips.total units: All homes in the development, restricted and unrestricted.
tips.li units: Low-income units — the homes restricted to income-qualified households under the tax-credit agreement.
tips.% of li units: Share of the development's homes that are income-restricted.
tips.year pis: Year placed in service — when the development opened and its credits began.
tips.year allocated: Year CHFA awarded the tax credits.
tips.yr alloc: Year CHFA awarded the tax credits.
tips.credit type: 9% (competitive, awarded through the QAP) or 4% (paired with tax-exempt private-activity bonds).
tips.dda/qct *: Whether the site sits in a Difficult Development Area or Qualified Census Tract, which qualifies it for a 30% basis boost. See the note below the table.
tips.metro area: The metropolitan statistical area the county belongs to, where HUD publishes metro-level limits.
tips.current price: Most recent price in the series.
tips.subsidy type: The federal or state program whose affordability restriction applies — for example LIHTC, HUD Section 8, USDA Rural Development.
tips.owner type: Whether the owner is a for-profit, nonprofit, or public entity — nonprofit and public owners are less likely to leave a program at expiration.
tips.assisted units: Homes covered by the affordability restriction.
tips.expiration: When the current affordability restriction or subsidy contract ends — the point at which the homes could convert to market rate.
tips.stage: Where the opportunity sits in the pipeline, from screening to closed.
tips.next action: The concrete next step recorded for this opportunity.
tips.ioi: Indication of interest — a non-binding signal from a partner or funder.
tips.confidence: How much to trust the figure: high, medium, or low, with the reason stated where it is not high.
tips.dataset: The public dataset the site caches for this row.
tips.records: Number of records in the cached copy.
tips.data as of: The date the source publisher stamped on the data — its vintage, not the date it was fetched.
tips.cache age: How long ago the site last fetched the dataset.
tips.status: Current state of the row — for a dataset, whether it is fresh, stale, or failing; for a project or bill, where it stands.
tips.name: Name of the source or dataset.
tips.category: The kind of data the source provides.
tips.coverage: The geography and time range the dataset covers.
tips.format: File format the site stores the data in.
tips.freshness: Whether the cached copy is within its expected refresh window.
tips.last updated: When the cached copy was last refreshed.
tips.actions: Links to inspect, refresh, or open the source.
tips.local file: Where the cached copy lives in the repository.
tips.last refreshed: When the cached copy was last rebuilt.
tips.ami level: Percentage of area median income the row's limit applies to.
tips.1 person: Income limit for a one-person household at this AMI level.
tips.2 person: Income limit for a two-person household at this AMI level.
tips.3 person: Income limit for a three-person household at this AMI level.
tips.4 person: Income limit for a four-person household at this AMI level.
tips.1-person ami (100%): Area median income for a one-person household.
tips.4-person ami (100%): Area median income for a four-person household — HUD's reference household.
tips.60% ami max income: Highest income a four-person household can have and still qualify for a 60%-AMI tax-credit home.
tips.ami band: Income band as a share of area median income.
tips.affordable rent(4-person, 30% of income): Monthly rent a four-person household at this income could pay without exceeding 30% of income.
tips.priced-affordable units: Homes renting at or below the affordable rent for this band — occupied or not, and by anyone.
tips.gap (units − hh): Priced-affordable homes minus households in the band. Negative means more households than affordable homes.
tips.gap (units): Shortfall of affordable homes for the band: households minus homes renting at a price they can afford.
tips.coverage ratio: Priced-affordable homes divided by households in the band. Below 1.0 means a shortfall.
tips.supply coverage: Share of income-qualified households for whom a priced-affordable home exists.
tips.commitment date: Date the jurisdiction filed its Proposition 123 commitment with DOLA.
tips.acres: Size of the site or parcel in acres.
tips.zoning: Current zoning designation of the parcel.
tips.address: Street address of the site or property.
tips.studio: Studio homes — count or rent, as the table states.
tips.1br: One-bedroom homes — count or rent, as the table states.
tips.2br: Two-bedroom homes — count or rent, as the table states.
tips.3br: Three-bedroom homes — count or rent, as the table states.
tips.relative cost: This county's area median income compared with the statewide figure — above 1.0 means limits (and permitted rents) run higher than the state average.
tips.market: The metropolitan market the concession figures describe.
tips.avg concession: Average value of move-in incentives landlords are offering in this market, such as free weeks of rent.
tips.% of gross rent: The concession expressed as a share of the annual gross rent it discounts.
tips.free weeks equivalent: The concession restated as the number of weeks of free rent it is worth.
tips.primary driver: The main condition behind the concessions in this market — for example new supply delivering or slowing lease-up.
tips.present: Whether the item is in place for this jurisdiction, as of the source date shown.
tips.policy marker: A civic-capacity signal — an adopted plan, filing, ordinance or program — that funders and the QAP read as readiness.
tips.scope: The geography or rent segment a rent measure covers, so like is compared with like.
tips.use: How the figure is used in this analysis, or what the source is used for, as the table's caption explains.
tips.today: The current value, from the latest data vintage shown.
tips.+10yr: Projected value ten years out, under the growth scenario the table names.
tips.+20yr: Projected value twenty years out, under the growth scenario the table names.
tips.bedroom size: Home size by number of bedrooms; rents and income limits differ by size.
tips.fy2026 fmr / mo: HUD Fair Market Rent for fiscal year 2026 — the monthly rent HUD sets for this area and bedroom size, used as the ceiling for voucher payments and as a reference in tax-credit underwriting.
tips.ami %: Percentage of area median income the row's limit applies to.
tips.1-person: Income limit for a one-person household at this AMI level.
tips.2-person: Income limit for a two-person household at this AMI level.
tips.3-person: Income limit for a three-person household at this AMI level.
tips.4-person: Income limit for a four-person household at this AMI level.
tips.5-person: Income limit for a five-person household at this AMI level.
tips.6-person: Income limit for a six-person household at this AMI level.
tips.7-person: Income limit for a seven-person household at this AMI level.
tips.8-person: Income limit for an eight-person household at this AMI level.
